Doxycycline: Pfizer. It is used to treat bacterial pneumonia, acne, chlamydia infections, Lyme disease, cholera, typhus, and syphilis, and is sometimes used to prevent malaria.
In which country is St. Bernard?

St. Bernard (dog breed): Switzerland. The hospice, built by and named after the Alpine monk Saint Bernard of Menthon, 
acquired its first dogs between 1660 and 1670.
Who is credited with discovering General relativity?
General relativity: Albert Einstein. The relation is specified by the Einstein field equations, a system of second-order partial differential equations.
Who is credited with discovering Tetracycline?
Tetracycline: Lloyd Conover. It is available in oral and topical formulations.
Who is credited with discovering Potassium?
Potassium: Humphry Davy. Potassium is a chemical element; it has symbol K (from Neo-Latin kalium) and atomic number 19.
Made of adenine bonded to a sugar, this RNA building block underlies ATP, the cell's main energy currency, and doubles as an IV treatment for certain cardiac arrhythmias — what is it?
Adenosine (symbol A) is an organic compound that occurs widely in nature in the form of diverse derivatives.
The simplest pnictogen hydride, with the formula NH3, this pungent gas is also a common nitrogenous waste in living things — what is it?
Ammonia is an inorganic chemical compound of nitrogen and hydrogen with the formula NH3.
This emotion is defined by dread over events that haven't happened yet, distinguishing it from fear, which responds to a threat that's already present. What is it?
Anxiety is an emotion characterized by an unpleasant state of inner turmoil and includes feelings of dread over anticipated events.
This American psychologist developed the philosophy of radical behaviorism and pioneered operant conditioning while a longtime professor at Harvard — who is he?
B. F. Skinner (March 20, 1904 - August 18, 1990) was an American psychologist, behaviorist, inventor, and social philosopher.

First flickering to life in octocorals some 540 million years ago and evolving independently at least 94 separate times, this glow is sometimes borrowed from symbiotic bacteria — what is the phenomenon?
Bioluminescence is the production of light by an organism as the result of a chemiluminescence reaction.
Whose book Atlas of the Heart became an HBO Max documentary series in 2022, following an earlier Netflix film about her work on courage?
Brené Brown (born November 18, 1965) is an American academic, author and podcaster.
First classified by Linnaeus in 1753, which herbaceous annual takes its specific name from the Latin for 'cultivated' and has long supplied fiber, seed oil, food and medicine?
Cannabis sativa is an annual herbaceous flowering plant.

The scientific study of matter's properties and behavior, this physical science occupies an intermediate position between physics and biology, sometimes called the central science. What is this field of study?
Chemistry is the scientific study of the properties and behavior of matter. Chemistry also addresses the nature of chemical bonds in chemical compounds.
Once a standard topical anesthetic prized for narrowing blood vessels, this tropane alkaloid is extracted from the leaves of South American coca plants — which substance is it?
Cocaine is a central nervous system (CNS) stimulant and tropane alkaloid, derived primarily from the leaves of two coca species native to South America.
Native to North America and smaller than its close relative the gray wolf, this canine fills a similar ecological niche to the golden jackal of Eurasia — which animal?
Coyote (Canis latrans) is a species of canine also known as the American jackal, prairie wolf, and brush wolf.
Caused by either too little insulin or cells that ignore it, this condition keeps blood sugar stubbornly high and comes chiefly in a type 1 and a type 2 — what is it?
Diabetes is a group of common endocrine diseases characterized by sustained high blood sugar levels.
Which natural science examines how living things relate to their environment, spanning the individual, population, community, ecosystem, and biosphere levels?
Ecology (from Ancient Greek (okos) 'house' and - (-loga) 'study of') is the natural science of the relationships among living organisms and their environment.

Discovered in January 2005 by a Palomar Observatory team and named after a Greco-Roman goddess of strife, this trans-Neptunian object is the most massive known dwarf planet in the solar system — which one?
Eris (dwarf planet) (minor-planet number 136199) is the most massive and second-largest known dwarf planet in the Solar System.
This field of study, related to economics and business administration, is typically divided into personal, corporate, and public branches. What field is it?
Finance refers to monetary resources as well as the discipline that studies such resources, with related concepts such as money, currency, assets and liabilities.
Found on every continent except Antarctica, this lizard lacks eyelids — instead its eyeballs are covered by a transparent membrane called a brille. What is it?
Gecko are small, mostly carnivorous lizards that have a wide distribution, found on every continent except Antarctica.
Also called the woodchuck, this North American rodent is exceptional among its kin: while most marmots live in rocky mountains, this lowland burrower roams the Eastern U.S. into Alaska — what is it?
Groundhog (Marmota monax), also known as the woodchuck, is a rodent of the family Sciuridae, belonging to the group of large ground squirrels known as marmots.
A member of the human Herpesviridae family, this contagious pathogen comes in two types, with about 67% of people under 50 carrying the first as of 2016. What is it?
Herpes simplex virus (HSV-1 and HSV-2) are two members of the human Herpesviridae family, a set of viruses that produce viral infections in the majority of humans.

Literally meaning 'below mania,' this psychiatric condition brings a non-contextual elevation of mood along with increased energy, irritability, and impulsivity, but without the psychotic features of full mania — name this condition?
Hypomania (literally "below mania" or "less than mania") is a psychiatric condition of abnormally heightened mood and increased energy that is less severe than mania.
Part of the fig and mulberry family and thriving in tropical lowlands, this giant of the produce world can weigh as much as 55 kg and measures up to 90 cm long — what is it?
Jackfruit (Artocarpus heterophyllus) is a species of tree in the fig, mulberry, and breadfruit family (Moraceae).
This Mexican-American astronaut flew on STS-128, led a branch at Johnson Space Center, and — urged on by President Obama — ran for Congress in 2012; who is he?
José M. Hernández (born August 7, 1962) is a Mexican-American engineer and astronaut.
What reddish-brown, alcohol-based tincture of opium, roughly 10% opium by weight, was historically sold without a prescription as a pain reliever and cough suppressant until the early 20th century?
Laudanum is a tincture of opium containing approximately 10% powdered opium by weight (the equivalent of 1% morphine).
Used since pre-Columbian times as a pack animal that can haul about a quarter of its body weight for miles, which domesticated South American camelid has wool low in lanolin?
Llama (Spanish) (Lama glama) is a domesticated South American camelid, widely used as a meat and pack animal by Andean cultures since the pre-Columbian era.
Though it's the strongest bone in the face, this lower jawbone tends to deform with age and is prone to fractures — what is it called?

Mandible (from the Latin mandibula, 'for chewing'), lower jaw, or jawbone is a bone that makes up the lower - and typically more mobile - component of the mouth (the upper jaw being known as the maxilla).
Aristotle called this the 'first philosophy' — the branch that probes the most fundamental structure of reality, from existence itself to the categories of being — what is it?
Metaphysics is the branch of philosophy that examines the basic nature or most fundamental structure of reality.
Named for the river near which its type fossil was found by a Dutch chalk quarry in the 18th century, this genus of marine reptile lived until the end of the Cretaceous — what is it?
Mosasaurus ("lizard of the Meuse River") is the type genus (defining example) of the Mosasauridae, an extinct group of aquatic squamate reptiles.

An English aeronautical engineer who wrote novels like On the Beach and A Town Like Alice, he adopted a pen name specifically so his employers at Vickers wouldn't think him 'not a serious person.' Who is he?
Nevil Shute (17 January 1899 - 12 January 1960) was an English novelist and aeronautical engineer who spent his later years in Australia.
Its name means 'serpent-bearer' in Ancient Greek — this large constellation straddling the celestial equator is depicted as a man grasping a snake — name it?
Ophiuchus (o-fee-) is a large constellation straddling the celestial equator.
This English amateur astronomer joined an astronomy association at age 11, compiled the Caldwell catalogue, and hosted the BBC's record-breaking 'The Sky at Night' — who was he?
Patrick Moore (4 March 1923 - 9 December 2012) was an English amateur astronomer who attained prominence in that field as a writer, researcher, radio commentator and television presenter.

This branch of linguistics studies how languages organize their foundational sound units — like the contrast between 'bat' and 'gnat' — or, in sign languages, elements like hand shape and location — what is it called?
Phonology (formerly also phonemics or phonematics) is the branch of linguistics that concerns how languages organize the foundational elements that make their words.
Native to cool temperate regions of the Old World, which poplar species is commonly known as European or quaking aspen?
Populus tremula (commonly called aspen, common aspen, Eurasian aspen, European aspen, or quaking aspen) is a species of poplar native to cool temperate regions of the Old World.
Found in nucleic acids as the building block behind adenine and guanine, this nitrogen-rich heterocyclic compound is the most common of its kind in nature — what is it?
Purine is a heterocyclic aromatic organic compound that consists of two rings (pyrimidine and imidazole) fused together.
Home to about 200 species — among them the plants we call currants and gooseberries — this genus is the sole member of its own plant family — which genus?
Ribes is a genus of approximately 200 known species of flowering plants, predominantly native to the temperate regions of the Northern Hemisphere.
The FAO/WHO Codex standard recognizes 21 species under this common name for small silvery forage fish, distinguished from their larger 'pilchard' cousins mainly by size — what fish is it?
Sardine are common names for various species of small, oily forage fish in the herring suborder Clupeoidei.

Defined by the American Thoracic Society as a subjective, uncomfortable experience of breathing discomfort that can include chest tightness or a sense of effort to breathe — what is this sensation called?
Shortness of breath (SOB), known as dyspnea (in AmE) or dyspnoea (in BrE), is an uncomfortable feeling of not being able to breathe well enough.

This class of moisture-loving hexapods — the largest lineage of six-legged creatures excluded from the insect group — indirectly aids decomposition by breaking down organic matter and shaping soil microbial life. What are they?
Springtail (class Collembola) form the largest of the three lineages of modern hexapods that are no longer considered insects, the others being Protura and Diplura.

This genus of about a dozen woody flowering shrubs in the olive family, native from southeastern Europe to East Asia, is closely related to privet and provides food for several moth larvae — what is it commonly called?
Syringa is a genus of 12 currently recognized species of flowering woody plants in the olive family called lilacs.
Known in medical Latin as the pollex, this digit sits outermost on the hand when you stand palms-forward — which body part?
Thumb is the first digit of the hand, next to the index finger.
The two major groups of these reptiles, side-necked and hidden-necked, differ in how they pull in the head — and they breathe air despite many living in water. What animal?
Turtle (order Testudines) are reptiles characterized by a special shell developed mainly from their ribs, as well as keratinized toothless beak.
One of the oldest leaf vegetables eaten by humans, this fast-growing aquatic plant in the cabbage family shares its peppery bite with relatives like mustard, radish, and wasabi — what plant is it?
Watercress (Nasturtium officinale) is a species of aquatic flowering plant in the cabbage family, Brassicaceae.

This paraphilia describes a sexual fixation on non-human animals, distinct from acting on such attraction, and was estimated in one 2021 study to affect about 2 percent of the population — name the term?
Zoophilia is a paraphilia in which a person experiences a sexual fixation on non-human animals.
This practice leans on 'branding' — tying a name or image to certain qualities in people's minds — to nudge them toward buying more. What field is it?
Advertising: Form of communication for marketing.
This Swedish chemist held 355 patents, invented dynamite, and then left his fortune to fund a famous set of prizes. Who was he?
Alfred Nobel: Swedish chemist and inventor (1833–1896)
Ectothermic four-limbed vertebrates whose only living members are frogs, salamanders, and the worm-like caecilians — what class of animal is this?
Amphibian: Class of ectothermic tetrapods. The origin of modern lissamphibians, which first appeared during the Early Triassic, around 250 million years ago, has long been contentious.
Nicknamed 'Nastia' in the USSR and known to NATO as 'Curl,' this twin-engine turboprop military transport was later license-built in China under a different name — what aircraft is it?
Antonov An-26: Soviet turboprop transport aircraft. It is the third member of the Antonov An-24 family, coming after the An-24 and An-30, while preceding the An-32 and cancelled An-132.
Ranking as the second-largest lizard species after the Komodo dragon, this excellent swimmer thrives in lakes, rivers, and even city sewers across South and Southeast Asia — what is it?
Asian water monitor: Species of lizard. The Asian water monitor (Varanus salvator) is a large varanid lizard native to South and Southeast Asia.
As the largest member of the grass family, one species of this plant can grow stalks over 46 meters tall and 36 centimeters thick — name the plant?
Bamboo: Subfamily of plants in the grass family.
Both heads of this upper-arm muscle originate on the scapula and let you flex your elbow while turning your palm upward — what muscle is it?

Biceps: Muscle on the front of the upper arm. While the long head of the biceps crosses both the shoulder and elbow joints, its main function is at the elbow where it flexes and supinates the forearm.

Flying for the U.S. Air Force since 1955, this subsonic strategic bomber evolved from a six-turboprop straight-wing design into eight swept-wing turbojets and can haul up to 70,000 pounds of weapons — what's its name?
Boeing B-52 Stratofortress: American strategic bomber aircraft.

This Italian-American physicist invented an improved coincidence circuit and traveled to Eritrea to prove cosmic rays arrive more strongly from the West than the East, before Italy's racial laws forced him to flee — who was he?
When this yeast infection strikes the mouth it's commonly called thrush, leaving telltale white patches on the tongue — what is the condition?
Candidiasis: Fungal infection due to any type of Candida.
Responsible for nearly 40 percent of blindness cases worldwide in 2020, this condition clouds the eye's lens and causes halos around lights — which condition?
Cataract: Clouding of the lens inside the eye, causing poor vision.
Named for both the tree and its edible nut, this genus of temperate deciduous trees belongs to the beech family — what is it?
Chestnut: Genus of plants. The name also refers to the edible nuts they produce.
This English inventor made the world's first slimline pocket calculator in 1972, then launched the UK's first mass-market home computer for under £100 — who is he?
Clive Sinclair: English entrepreneur and inventor (1940–2021)
A heavy-set, fox-like canid native to East Asia, this animal is named for its raccoon-like face markings and is unusual among canids for hibernating in winter and climbing trees. What is this animal?
Common raccoon dog: Canid indigenous to East Asia. Named for its raccoon-like face markings, it is most closely related to foxes.
First described in 1963, this rare disorder from a partial deletion on chromosome 5 gets its French name from the distinctive feline-sounding cry of affected infants — what is it called?
Cri du chat syndrome: Human medical condition.

This English broadcaster is the only person to have won BAFTA Awards in black-and-white, colour, high-definition, 3D, and 4K — a span made possible by a presenting career that began with Zoo Quest in 1954. Who is this natural historian?
David Attenborough: English broadcaster and natural historian (born 1926)

A lean, wedge-skulled medium canine found in Australia and split off from the New Guinea singing dog, this animal's very classification — dog, wolf, or its own species — is still hotly debated — what is it?
Dingo: Canid species native to Australia.

Anatomically like us, some of the oldest remains of this species come from Ethiopia's Omo-Kibish site, dated to roughly 233,000 to 196,000 years ago — what term distinguishes them from archaic humans?
Early modern human: Old Stone Age ''Homo sapiens''
This inner lining of the uterus sheds during menstruation but thickens dramatically to help form the placenta during pregnancy — what is it?
Endometrium: Lining of the mammalian uterus. It has a basal layer and a functional layer: the basal layer contains stem cells which regenerate the functional layer.
This warbler's head marking gives it its name — dark in the male, chestnut in the female — and its closest relative is the garden warbler. What bird is it?
Eurasian blackcap: Bird in the Old World warbler family from Eurasia and Africa.

Colloquially called squirting or gushing, this fluid is expelled from the Skene's gland near the urethra around the time of orgasm — and researchers stress it's physiologically distinct from coital incontinence. What is it?
Female ejaculation: Expulsion of fluid during orgasm.
Named for hindwings that resemble human ears when unfolded, this reddish-brown insect is a common household pest known for the pincers at the tip of its abdomen — which species?
Forficula auricularia: Species of earwig. It is an omnivorous insect belonging to the family Forficulidae.
Nicknamed the 'stomach flu' in the US and Canada, this inflammation of the gut is most often caused in kids by rotavirus and in adults by norovirus — what is it?
Gastroenteritis: Inflammation of the stomach and small intestine.
Occurring mainly in the liver, this metabolic pathway builds new glucose from non-carbohydrate sources to help prevent low blood sugar — what is it called?
This Dutch programmer created a popular programming language and held the title 'benevolent dictator for life' until stepping down in 2018. Who is he?
Guido van Rossum: Dutch programmer and creator of Python (born 1956)
Tapeworms, flukes and roundworms all fall under this broad name for any infection where parasitic worms take up residence in the body. What is the condition called?
Helminthiasis: Any macroparasitic disease caused by helminths.
Belonging to the genus Apis, this eusocial insect builds perennial nests of hexagonal wax cells and stores surplus food as a prized sweet — which creature is it?
This psychiatric state brings a surge of energy, euphoria, and a reduced need for sleep — milder than its more severe cousin because it doesn't significantly impair daily functioning — what is it?

A former Communist Party official who was later sidelined by Nicolae Ceaușescu, this engineer-turned-politician emerged from Romania's 1989 revolution to become the country's first freely elected president — who is he?
After a cross-country road trip from New York to Seattle, this Princeton engineering graduate founded an online bookstore in 1994 that grew into a global e-commerce giant. Who is he?
This twin-engine fighter jet program made its home nation the fourth in the world to develop stealth avionics, joining the ranks of the US, China, and Russia — which aircraft?
KAI KF-21 Boramae: South Korean fighter aircraft.

Until a 2020 taxonomic overhaul split many of its 261 species into 25 new genera, this rod-shaped, gram-positive bacterial genus formed a major part of the human gut and vaginal microbiota — what genus?
Lactobacillus: Genus of bacteria. Lactobacillus forms biofilms in the vaginal and gut microbiota, allowing them to persist in harsh environmental conditions and maintain ample populations.
This Chinese herbalist, martial artist, and tactical advisor died in 1933 having allegedly been born in 1677 — a longevity claim gerontologists dismiss as myth. Who was he?
Li Ching-Yuen: Chinese herbalist (died 1933). Li's year of birth was alleged to be 1677, though his true age has never been determined.
This Berkeley professor gave us "fuzzy" everything — fuzzy sets, fuzzy logic, fuzzy control — proposing a whole branch of mathematics for reasoning with imprecision. Who was he?
Defined by milk-producing glands, hair or fur, a broad neocortex, and three tiny middle-ear bones, this animal class split from reptile-and-bird ancestors over 300 million years ago — what is it?
Mammal: Class of animals with milk-producing glands.

Marked by small white Koplik spots inside the mouth and a red rash that starts on the face before spreading, this highly contagious, vaccine-preventable disease can bring fevers over 40°C — which disease?
This development economist shared the 2019 Nobel with Esther Duflo and Abhijit Banerjee for an experimental approach to fighting global poverty — who is he?
Michael Kremer: American economist and Nobel laureate (born 1964)
Named in 1883 by a German anthropologist who wrongly believed it was most common among his patients, this bluish congenital birthmark usually fades by puberty — what is it?
Mongolian spot: Type of birthmark. It normally disappears three to five years after birth and almost always by puberty.

When light from distant objects focuses in front of the retina rather than on it, far-away things blur while close ones stay sharp — and spending more time outdoors as a child seems to lower the risk. What's this refractive error?
Myopia: Inability to focus on distant objects.
This small sauropod dinosaur had a wide muzzle packed with more than 500 teeth that were replaced roughly every two weeks — what genus is it?
Sold under the brand name Zyprexa, this atypical antipsychotic treats schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, and is sometimes used off-label to fight chemotherapy-induced nausea — what is this drug?
Olanzapine: Atypical antipsychotic medication. Olanzapine, sold under the brand name Zyprexa among others, is an atypical antipsychotic primarily used to treat schizophrenia and bipolar disorder.
Prized both as a delicacy and, in some species, for the pearls grown within its shell, which salt-water bivalve is this?
Oyster: Variety of families of Mollusca.
This hickory species native to the Mississippi River region produces a nut used in praline candy and a famous holiday pie, and is the official state tree of Texas — what is it?
Pecan: Species of nut tree native to the southern USA and northern Mexico.

First described by Carl Ludwig Koch in 1850, this family of over 2,000 araneomorph spiders includes the "cellar spider" and "vibrating spider" — and shares a famous leggy nickname with harvestmen and crane flies. What family is it?
Pholcidae: Family of spiders. The family, first described by Carl Ludwig Koch in 1850, is divided into 94 genera.
Sometimes called a 'collapsed lung,' this condition involves air trapped in the space between the lung and chest wall, causing sudden sharp one-sided chest pain — what is it?
Pneumothorax: Abnormal collection of air in the pleural space.
This beta blocker treats high blood pressure and performance anxiety alike, and can even shrink capillary hemangiomas in infants — what drug?
Propranolol: Beta blocker drug. It can be taken orally, rectally, or by intravenous injection.
First identified in the 1950s as a radio source, this extremely luminous galactic nucleus can outshine an entire galaxy like the Milky Way thousands of times over — what is it?
Quasar: Active galactic nucleus (AGN) containing a supermassive black hole.
Often compared to the film in a camera, this innermost, light-sensitive layer of the eye sends signals along the optic nerve to the visual cortex — what is it?
Retina: Part of the eye. The retina (from Latin rete 'net'; pl. retinae or retinas) is the innermost, light-sensitive layer of tissue of the eye.
Discovered in 1973 by Ruth Bishop via electron micrograph images, this fecal-oral pathogen is the leading cause of diarrheal illness in infants worldwide — which pathogen?
Rotavirus: Specific genus of RNA viruses.
Found in every ocean but never in fresh water, most of these bivalves can swim in rapid bursts across the seafloor rather than staying put — which shellfish?
Scallop: Family of shellfish, many edible.
This body of religious law, drawn from the Qur'an and hadith, refers to immutable divine law — distinct from fiqh, its human interpretation by scholars. What is it?
Sharia: Islamic law. Approaches to Sharia in the 21st century vary widely, and the role and mutability of Sharia in a changing world has become an increasingly debated topic in Islam.
A hygroscopic crystalline powder (formula NaNO2) and the most industrially important salt of its kind, this compound is most familiar to us cured into processed meats. What is it?
Sodium nitrite: Chemical compound. It is a white to slightly yellowish crystalline powder that is very soluble in water and is hygroscopic.
This Polish-American DuPont chemist invented a super-strong polymer fiber and became the fourth woman ever inducted into the National Inventors Hall of Fame — who was she?
Stephanie Kwolek: American chemist who invented Kevlar (1923–2014)
Commonly known as fainting, this fast-onset, short-duration loss of consciousness and muscle strength is typically caused by a sudden drop in blood flow to the brain — what's the medical term?
Syncope (medicine): Transient loss of consciousness and postural tone.
Also called oxolane, this colorless, water-miscible cyclic ether is a versatile solvent and polymer precursor — and an isomer of butanone. Abbreviated with three letters, what is it?
Discovered in Cornwall in 1791 and named after the Titans of Greek myth, this corrosion-resistant transition metal shrugs off seawater, aqua regia, and chlorine alike — what is it?
Titanium: Chemical element with atomic number 22 (Ti)
Roughly three times stiffer than steel and nearly as hard as diamond, this gray powder is sintered into cutting tools, armor-piercing bullets, and jewelry — what compound is it?
Tungsten carbide: Hard, dense and stiff chemical compound.
The brightest star in the constellation Lyra, this star sits just 25 light-years away and served as Earth's northern pole star around 12,000 BCE — which star?
Vega: Brightest star in the constellation Lyra. It has the Bayer designation α Lyrae, which is Latinised to Alpha Lyrae and abbreviated Alpha Lyr or α Lyr.
With a distinctive pale eye and grey nape against black plumage, this small, gregarious member of the crow family was first formally described by Linnaeus — name the bird?
Western jackdaw: Species of bird in the crow family Corvidae.
As Jimmy Carter's National Security Advisor from 1977 to 1981, this Polish-American scholar organized the Trilateral Commission and oversaw normalized ties with Communist China — who was he?
Zbigniew Brzezinski: Polish-American diplomat and political scientist (1928–2017)
What is the chemical symbol for astatine?
The symbol for astatine is At. Astatine is a chemical element; it has symbol At and atomic number 85.
Rutherfordium is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for rutherfordium is Rf. Rutherfordium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Rf and atomic number 104.

In what year was Kris Jenner born?
Kris Jenner: Kristen Mary Jenner (née Houghton HOH-tən, formerly Kardashian; born November 5, 1955) is an American media personality, socialite, and businesswoman.
In what year was Simon Cowell born?
Simon Cowell: Simon Phillip Cowell (born 7 October 1959) is an English television personality, record executive, and entrepreneur.
In what year was Shia LaBeouf born?
Shia LaBeouf: Shia Saide LaBeouf (SHY-ə lə-BUF; born June 11, 1986) is an American actor and filmmaker.
In what year was Woody Harrelson born?
Woody Harrelson: Woodrow Tracy Harrelson (born July 23, 1961) is an American actor.

Keri Russell: Keri Lynn Russell (born March 23, 1976) is an American actress.
In what year was Christopher Nolan born?
Christopher Nolan: Sir Christopher Edward Nolan (born 30 July 1970) is a British and American filmmaker.

Donnie Yen: Yen made his American debut in Highlander: Endgame (2000), followed by a cameo in Blade II (2002).
In what year was Armie Hammer born?
Armie Hammer: Armand Douglas Hammer (born August 28, 1986) is an American actor.
In what year was Chloë Grace Moretz born?
Chloë Grace Moretz ( mə-RETS; born February 10, 1997) is an American actress.
In what year was Katharine Hepburn born?
Katharine Hepburn: Katharine Houghton Hepburn (May 12, 1907 – June 29, 2003) was an American actress whose career as a leading lady on stage and screen spanned six decades.
In what year was Walt Disney born?
Walt Disney: Walter Elias Disney ( DIZ-nee; December 5, 1901 – December 15, 1966) was an American animator, film producer, voice actor, and entrepreneur.
In what year did John Candy die?
John Candy: John Franklin Candy (October 31, 1950 – March 4, 1994) was a Canadian actor and comedian best known for his work in Hollywood comedy films.
In what year was Terrifier 2 first released?
Terrifier 2 is a 2022 American independent supernatural slasher film written, edited, co-produced, and directed by Damien Leone.
In what year was The Last Voyage of the Demeter first released?
The Last Voyage of the Demeter: It is an adaptation of "The Captain's Log", a chapter from the 1897 novel Dracula by Bram Stoker.

In what year was Meg 2: The Trench first released?

In what year was Wish first released?
Wish is a 2023 American animated musical fantasy film produced by Walt Disney Animation Studios.
In what year was Nefarious first released?
Nefarious (film): It stars Jordan Belfi as a psychiatrist who must determine if a convicted death row inmate (Sean Patrick Flanery) is faking his alleged demonic possession.
